goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test changes or validation evidence

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is too vague and not a verifiable defect in this diff. The diff does include multiple relevant test updates/additions (e.g., new specs for `EmbeddableHost`, updated `embed_controller_spec`, `topic_embed_spec`, and new admin controller specs). While not every new behavior (like the Ember store `_hydrateEmbedded` change) is explicitly covered by tests, the diff does not show an obvious missing/required test change that would clearly break or regress correctness on its own. Therefore this finding does not identify a concrete, demonstrable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:7-9 crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site setting is absent from the database, because execute(...)[0] is nil and nil['id'].to_i raises an error, making the fallback to uncategorized_category_id on line 11 unreachable

Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the Fabricator(:category), :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category definitions

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that the contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, detailing that category_fabricator.rb now contains only the embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category-related fabricators. This matches the golden issue about swapped files and loss/misplacement of original category fabricators leading to potential errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22 uses unsafe string interpolation in SQL INSERT statement, which will fail or produce incorrect data if host values contain single quotes or special SQL characters

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the loop does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The `h` value comes from `site_settings.value` (`embeddable_hosts`) and is interpolated directly into a SQL string with surrounding single quotes and no escaping/quoting. If any host line contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), the migration can fail with a SQL syntax error or insert corrupted data; in the worst case it enables SQL injection during migration execution. This is a concrete defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting is blank or missing because the fallback check comes after the query that crashes

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration does `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i`. If there is no `site_settings` row for `embed_category` (common when the setting was never customized) or if it’s blank / doesn’t match any category name, `execute(...)` returns an empty result, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. The fallback `if category_id == 0` is reached only after the `.to_i`, so it cannot prevent the crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil host not handled in controller update and destroy actions, causing NoMethodError when host doesn't exist
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue highlights that the controller’s update and destroy actions don’t handle a nil host when the record isn’t found, leading to NoMethodError—same core problem as the golden comment (missing existence check after lookup by ID).

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? no longer validates that embeddable hosts are configured, causing behavioral regression where topics are considered expandable without any configured hosts

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Topic#expandable_first_post?` changes from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. However, `embeddable_hosts` as a SiteSetting is removed entirely (from `site_settings.yml`, server locale docs, and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` is deleted) and replaced by the `EmbeddableHost` model + DB-backed configuration. Also, `expandable_first_post?` still requires `has_topic_embed?`, so it does not make arbitrary topics expandable “without any configured hosts”; only topics that already have a `TopicEmbed` can be expandable. Whether existing embedded topics should stop being expandable when the allowed-host list is emptied is not a clear correctness requirement demonstrated by the diff, so the claimed “behavioral regression” is not a verifiable defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection risk in migration due to direct interpolation of host values from site_settings into SQL statements
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same core vulnerability: building SQL by directly interpolating host values into the query string, which creates a SQL injection risk. The candidate differs on where it occurs (mentions a migration vs. the specified controller file), but the underlying issue (unsafe interpolation instead of parameter binding/quoting) matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness validation on EmbeddableHost#host, allowing duplicate hosts and causing ambiguity in record_for_host

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the new EmbeddableHost model only validates format (`validates_format_of :host`) and the migration creates `embeddable_hosts.host` without a unique index. The admin controller `save_host` also does not prevent duplicates. As a result, duplicate rows for the same host can be created, and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` resolves with `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which becomes order-dependent/ambiguous if multiple records exist (potentially selecting the wrong category for embedding).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing JavaScript model definitions for 'embedding' and 'embeddable-host' that the Ember store needs to resolve these types
Controller specs only verify class inheritance, not CRUD behavior, leaving core functionality unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) and each contains only a single example asserting the controller inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. Meanwhile, the new controllers implement behavior (`create/update/destroy` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `show/update` in `Admin::EmbeddingController`), but none of that CRUD/endpoint behavior is exercised or asserted in these specs. So the finding accurately describes an unverified core functionality in the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op because the embedding object is an OpenStruct and nothing is persisted

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, `fetch_embedding` sets `@embedding` to an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...`. The `update` action does not modify any persisted state; it simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, so a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` cannot save anything. This matches the finding: the object is not an AR model and nothing is persisted in `update` (and there is no code in `update` that would persist changes elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files are swapped: the embeddable_host fabricator is in category_fabricator.rb and category fabricators are in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
Migration will crash with NoMethodError when the embed_category setting is absent, as indexing [0]['id'] on an empty result fails before the fallback check

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` on the result of an INNER JOIN that can legitimately return zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` missing from `site_settings`, blank/default, or not matching any category name). When zero rows are returned, `[0]` is `nil`, so `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. This is a real crash path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that ignores parameters and fails to save embedding settings

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists anything. This is verifiable in the diff: `fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` (not an AR model), so there is nothing to save, and `update` performs no mutation. On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, implying a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` should apply changes; however the server `update` is a no-op and will ignore any parameters. Therefore, if any embedding settings were intended to be saved via this endpoint, they won’t be.

adjudication_records.issue_text: General store infrastructure changes for pluralized embedded-ID hydration exceed the stated scope and affect all models

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make a global change to `store.js`’s `_hydrateEmbedded` to also hydrate keys ending in `_ids` (plural) by mapping IDs to records and deleting the original `*_ids` key. However, the proposed finding claims this is a “problem” because it “exceeds the stated scope” and “affects all models,” which is not a verifiable defect from the diff itself: there is no stated scope in the diff, and a global infrastructure change is not inherently incorrect. The change appears intentional to support the new `has_many ... embed: :ids` usage in `EmbeddingSerializer`, so the finding is too vague/general and does not identify a clear bug/security/correctness issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: type.replace('_', '-') in rest adapter changes behavior for all admin models, potentially causing unintended path resolution changes for types with underscores

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `basePath(store, type)` to compare `type.replace('_','-')` against the `ADMIN_MODELS` list, which now includes `embeddable-host`. This is a targeted compatibility change so underscored model names like `embeddable_host` or `site_customization` map to their dash-form entries and correctly resolve to `/admin/`. There’s no concrete evidence in the diff of an unintended path resolution bug being introduced—only the intended behavior change for those admin models. The finding is framed as a general “potentially unintended” risk without a verifiable failure case in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes when embed_category is never set because execute(...)[0] returns nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, making the fallback unreachable.
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the migration accessing the first result of execute(...) without verifying any rows exist, leading to a crash (nil/empty result then indexing ['id'] fails) when embed_category was never set, breaking the related feature path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection vulnerability in migration due to direct string interpolation of the host value into the INSERT statement instead of using parameterized queries.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads embeddable_hosts from the database and then builds SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` is not escaped or parameterized, so a host containing a single quote would break the SQL, and a crafted value could inject additional SQL. Even though the source is an existing site_setting, this is still a verifiable injection/escaping defect in the diff (unsafe raw SQL construction).

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true in create_table silently drops existing embeddable_hosts table and its data without warning if the migration is re-run or the table exists.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will issue a DROP TABLE (typically `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS embeddable_hosts`) before recreating it. That means if the table already exists for any reason (e.g., a partially applied migration, a manually created table, or an environment where migrations are rerun without a proper rollback), existing data would be silently discarded. This behavior is directly implied by the `force: true` option in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration is irreversible and destructively deletes source site_settings without a def down to restore them, and mixes data migration with DDL lacking error handling.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `def change` but performs non-reversible data operations via `execute` (selecting from `site_settings`, inserting rows into `embeddable_hosts`, and finally `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). Rails cannot automatically infer how to reverse these raw SQL mutations, so rolling back this migration will raise an irreversible migration error and the deleted `site_settings` values cannot be restored because no `down`/`reversible` logic is provided. This is a concrete, verifiable rollback/destructiveness problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unique constraint or validation on host allows duplicate host entries, causing ambiguity in record_for_host resolution.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `embeddable_hosts` table and `EmbeddableHost` model without any `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and without a DB unique index on `host`. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` resolves by `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so if duplicate rows exist for the same host (e.g., via admin UI or migration inserts), which record/category is chosen becomes arbitrary, creating ambiguous behavior (both for `host_allowed?` and for selecting `category_id` in `TopicEmbed.import`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host is not downcased before validation, allowing Example.com and example.com to coexist as separate rows and bypassing future uniqueness constraints.
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the host value isn’t consistently normalized (downcased) before being used, leading to case-sensitive mismatches/duplicates. The golden focuses on lookup failing despite `lower(host)=?`, while the candidate frames it as validation/uniqueness allowing separate rows, but the root cause is the same lack of downcasing the input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No foreign key constraint on category_id to categories table, risking dangling references when categories are deleted.

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates `embeddable_hosts` with a `category_id` column (`null: false`) but does not add any database foreign key constraint to `categories`. The model declares `belongs_to :category`, but that does not enforce referential integrity at the DB level. Therefore, if a category is deleted (or `category_id` is set to a non-existent id), `embeddable_hosts.category_id` can become a dangling reference, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing functional index on lower(host) for the hot-path query in record_for_host, causing a full table scan on every embed view request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and this is used on the embed request hot path (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`). The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table but defines no index on `host` (and certainly no functional index on `lower(host)`), so this lookup cannot use an index and will require a sequential scan as the table grows. This is a real, verifiable performance issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that silently discards all submitted embedding-level settings while appearing to save them.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action does not read or apply any submitted params; it simply re-renders the current `@embedding` (`render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`) which is built in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will issue a PUT but sends no meaningful payload and the server ignores any payload anyway. This makes the endpoint effectively a no-op that returns success-looking JSON without persisting embedding-level changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil-safety errors in EmbeddableHostsController where queries can return nil and raise NoMethodError on destroy/save, and params[:embeddable_host] can be nil without guards.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If the `id` is missing/invalid, this returns `nil`, after which `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...` (raising `NoMethodError`), and `destroy` will call `host.destroy` (also `NoMethodError`). Additionally, `save_host` unconditionally dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]`, so if `params[:embeddable_host]` is absent/malformed the code will raise. These are concrete nil-safety/correctness issues visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files are swapped, placing the :embeddable_host fabricator in category_fabricator.rb and category fabricators in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, causing maintainability confusion.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff removes the category fabricators from `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` and replaces that file with a `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while the new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the various `:category` fabricators. This is a verifiable mismatch between filenames and their contents (they are effectively swapped), which is confusing and makes the test fabricators harder to find/maintain, even if it may not immediately break execution if all fabricator files are loaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host returns inconsistent types (false vs nil vs record) for different failure conditions, creating a subtle bug source for future callers.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` method, failure paths explicitly `return false` (when URI parsing fails or host is missing), while the success path returns `where(...).first`, which yields an `EmbeddableHost` record or `nil` if not found. This means the method can return `false`, `nil`, or a record depending on the condition, which is an inconsistent contract and a real correctness/API defect introduced by the diff (even if current callers happen to tolerate it via `present?`/`try`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: _focusOnInput observer fires when leaving edit mode (editing transitions to false), targeting a non-existent DOM element and doing unnecessary afterRender work.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `_focusOnInput` is both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`, so it will run when `editing` changes to `false`. In the template, the `.host-name` input only exists in the `{{#if editing}}` branch, so when leaving edit mode the selector `this.$('.host-name')` will return an empty jQuery set. However, calling `.focus()` on an empty jQuery set is a no-op (does not throw), so this does not create a verifiable bug—only a minor, harmless extra scheduled afterRender callback. That makes the finding more of an optimization/style nit than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection vulnerability in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:30 due to direct interpolation of host value into raw SQL INSERT statement instead of using parameterized queries or sanitize_sql

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Here `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` and is not quoted/escaped via the DB adapter. If `h` contains a single quote or SQL fragment, it can break the SQL and potentially inject additional SQL. Even if the value is typically admin-provided, this is still a concrete unsafe raw-SQL construction in the diff (and can also cause migration failures on unexpected input).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:13-15 because there is no guard for missing 'embed_category' site_setting, causing NoMethodError when query returns empty array

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when looking up `embed_category`. If that SELECT returns 0 rows (e.g., `site_settings` has no `embed_category` row, which is plausible on fresh installs or when the setting was never overridden), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. There is no guard before indexing into the result, so the migration can crash.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb is not reversible because data migration steps are not wrapped in reversible/up/down blocks, causing data loss of deleted site_settings rows on rollback

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` defines only a `change` method but performs non-reversible data operations via raw SQL: it copies data from `site_settings` into `embeddable_hosts` and then runs `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot infer how to reverse those `execute` statements, and even if the table drop were reversed, the deleted `site_settings` rows cannot be restored on rollback without an explicit `down`/`reversible` implementation. This makes rollback either impossible (IrreversibleMigration) or lossy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator contents are swapped between spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, with category fabricators in the embeddable_host file and vice versa

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines category-related fabricators and instead defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` plus other category variants (`:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). This is a verifiable swap/misplacement of fabricator definitions across the two files, which is likely unintended and can break tests if any specs require fabricators by file name rather than loading the whole directory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update action in app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:11-13 is a no-op that re-renders serialized @embedding without processing request parameters, silently doing nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (lines 11-13) simply re-renders `@embedding` via `render_serialized` and does not read or apply any request parameters. Since `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` (not persisted) and the serializer only exposes `id` plus `embeddable_hosts` ids, the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` endpoint cannot actually update anything; any client-sent changes would be ignored. This matches the finding that the update action is effectively a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection vulnerability in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:27 where the value `h` from `embeddable_hosts` is interpolated directly into a SQL INSERT statement without escaping or parameterization, bypassing model validation and allowing arbitrary SQL execution.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration reads `val` from the `site_settings` table (`embeddable_hosts`), splits it into `h`, and then runs `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. Because `h` is interpolated directly into a SQL string without escaping/quoting helpers or bind parameters, a value containing a single quote (or crafted SQL) could break the statement or inject additional SQL during migration. This also bypasses any ActiveRecord validation/sanitization since it writes via raw SQL.
